LESSON: FOLDING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Natural Systems and Processes
Topic 2.2: Folding
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Folding, part of Natural Systems and Processes in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How does folding influence our day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Folding together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: the skill of global awareness is promoted as the learner draws/describe tactile world map showing the

distribution of fold mountains.

● Creativity and imagination: the skill of making connections is promoted as the learner draws/describes tactile sketches of

resultant features of folding on the earth’s surface.

Values:
● Unity: Learner portrays team spirit as they take turns when brainstorming on the meaning of folding.

● Respect: Learner displays humility as they discuss on types of folds resulting from tectonic forces.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental Education: Learner discusses on the types of folds resulting from tectonic forces.

● Creativity: Learner draws the world map showing the distribution of fold mountains and display in class.

● Assertiveness: Learner debates on the significance of folding and the resultant features.
